LESSON: WRITING POSTURE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Writing posture
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing posture, part of Writing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we sit appropriately when writing? 2. Why sit upright when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify appropriate sitting posture when scribbling, drawing and writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing posture in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. sit appropriately when scribbling, colouring and writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing posture in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. consult on appropriate sitting posture when involved in pre-writing and writing experiences. ● Select the correct or preferred sitting posture when writing from a variety of pictures, ● Observe demonstrated appropriate sitting posture when writing either from the teacher or a video clip, ● In purposive pair/grouping practices the correct writing posture after demonstration, ● In purposive pairs, practises the correct writing posture, ● Freely model objects using either clay, dough or plasticine while using correct sitting posture in preparation for writing. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted assistive technology or be supported to perform the task. ● Recite a simple poem on appropriate sitting posture while using actions. Learners with 1. How do we sit appropriately when writing? 2. Why sit upright when writing? 18 speech difficulties could use residual speech to recite the poem. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing posture together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
